speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of self-resolving knee pain followed by wrist pain and a recent camping trip in Minnesota is very concerning for Lyme disease. Given your sexual activity, could you describe the appearance and location of your skin lesions, and do you remember any tick bites during your trip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lesions you describe as "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" on your wrists and hands, combined with a prior knee history and recent camping, are highly suggestive of a specific arthropod-borne infection. Have you noticed any joint pain in your fingers or ankles in the last few days, and do you recall any tick bites during your camping trip? REQUEST TEST: Lyme Serology (ELISA)
